sana: Hey team — Customer 'AcmeMaps' on Dedicated (pool eu-prod-reserved-7) is seeing sustained 429s during their nightly vectorize job. They say it used to be fine at ~280 qps, but since last deploy they're pegged at ~230 qps and getting `429: rate_limit` with X-RateLimit-Remaining=0. Can someone triage?

jordan: On it. Do we have a request sample / headers and the customer's reserved commit?

sana: Sample response headers from their client: `x-rw-rl-limit: 300`, `x-rw-rl-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-rl-reset: 13s`, `content-length: 0`. Their reserved pool shows capacity 300 qps in the console, SLA is 300 qps sustained. They say burst used to allow short spikes to 380 qps.

alex: Quick question — are they hitting pool-level token accounting or per-route shaping? If the pool has a per-customer smoothing policy we might be converting bursts into sustained lower throughput.

sana: They were routed to that pool via dedicated mapping rule `route: acct-acmemaps -> eu-prod-reserved-7`. No recent changes on the account mapping. They provided repro steps:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIKEY" -d '{"input":"...large batch..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
# run in loop: for i in {1..600}; do curl ...; done
```

and client-side shows `429` after ~12-15s into the loop.

ops-bot: [alert] Dedicated pool eu-prod-reserved-7: sustained 95% utilization for 12m; rate-limiter fallback triggered. Incident: https://redwood.incidents/INC-3821

kevin: I'll check the rate-limiter instance set for that pool. Two possibilities: (1) the token-bucket max burst parameter got lowered in the last config push; (2) the pool's headroom reservation for system traffic is higher than intended. Both would reduce observed burst capacity.

alex: Also confirm the limiter granularity (per-second vs per-minute windows). If limiter is using a per-minute window and we enforce a strict average, short bursts will be throttled. We shipped a smoothing change last week that changes short-window burst allowance — could be the culprit.

jordan: Sana — can you ask customer for a recent raw request trace (ids) and exact timestamps? I want to correlate with rate-limiter logs. If they can run the repro with `?trace=true` on a dev key that would help.

sana: Sent a quick repro token and trace to support. They ran: `for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?trace=true; done` — and attached a trace snippet showing many requests return `x-rw-rl-remaining: 0` after 230 qps avg.

maria: Billing note: Their committed capacity is 600k tokens/month with a reserved qps mapping of 300. That billing commit shouldn't induce soft-blocking 429s — unless they exhausted an overlay quota (e.g., per-route soft guard). I'll cross-check overlay quotas for embeddings route.

kevin: Found config mismatch on the pool: last deploy set `burst_window_ms=200` instead of `2000` for the limiter due to a units bug in the config templating. That would make bursts very small and explain the drop from ~380 to ~230. I'm rolling a quick config fix to `burst_window_ms=2000` to restore previous behavior. Patching now to eu-prod-reserved-7.

alex: If you can, also re-run the synthetic loop against a canary instance after patch to confirm. Suggest running: `wrk -t2 -c50 -d30s -s ./emb-test.lua --  <endpoint>` or use the customer's loop.

ops-bot: [deploy] Config patch queued: cfgsvc/rl-burst-fix -> deployed to eu-prod-reserved-7 (rev: rl-burst-fix-2026-03-05). Link: https://consolesvc/configs/rl-burst-fix

kevin: Patch applied. Increasing burst_window_ms to 2000 and bumping burst_tokens cap to previous value. Observed immediate increase in allowed short bursts on canary: sustained 320-360 qps for 60s with occasional healthy backoff.

jordan: Sana, please have customer rerun repro. If they still see 429s, collect trace ids and we will pull RL logs.

sana: Customer reran and reports RPS jumped back to ~360 for 90s and 429s disappeared. They note one spike of `x-rw-rl-reset: 1s` during the transition but otherwise OK. They asked: can we add an alert when burst_window or burst_tokens deviate from pool baseline?

alex: Yes — we should add a config drift alert for critical pool parameters (burst_window_ms, burst_tokens, headroom). I'll open a ticket for the observability team.

maria: For completeness, I'm checking whether any billing enforcement flag flipped. Nothing there. I'll follow up if anything odd appears.

kevin: Root cause: templating bug in config pipeline that treated `ms` field as `seconds` in one rendering path. Gate added on deploy pipeline to validate critical rate-limiter fields now.

sana: Marking as resolved for the customer — will keep ticket open 48h to ensure no recurrence. Repro notes attached in ticket: run the curl loop, observe headers `x-rw-rl-limit`, `x-rw-rl-remaining`, `x-rw-rl-reset`. If 429 occurs, collect trace=true outputs and ping #support with trace ids. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Thx all — good catch. Closing escalation after post-mortem and alerting change.

kevin: Will follow up with a small postmortem summarizing the templating bug and config guard.

ops-bot: [note] Related incident INC-3821 updated with remediation details.
